14380.subject: Music
14380.question_text:
Define the following musical elements and explain their roles in a composition:
(i) Dynamics
(ii) Tempo
(iii) Timbre
14380.explanation:
(i) Dynamics refer to the volume of sound in music, indicated by symbols such as p (piano) for soft and f (forte) for loud. They add expressiveness and emotional depth to a composition.
(ii) Tempo is the speed of a piece, often indicated by terms like Allegro (fast) or Adagio (slow). It shapes the mood and energy of the music.
(iii) Timbre (or tone color) distinguishes different instruments or voices, even when playing the same pitch. It enriches texture and variety in a composition.

14381.subject: Music
14381.question_text:
Write the following notes in the treble clef:
(i) Middle C
(ii) E above middle C
(iii) G below middle C
Label each note with its letter name and octave designation (e.g., C4).
14381.explanation:
(i) Middle C is written on the first ledger line below the treble clef staff and is labeled C4.
(ii) E above middle C is the first line of the treble clef staff and is labeled E4.
(iii) G below middle C is written on the second space below the treble clef staff and is labeled G3.

14382.subject: Music
14382.question_text: Which of the following scales is not a type of diatonic scale?
14382.explanation: The chromatic scale is not a diatonic scale because it includes all twelve pitches within an octave, unlike diatonic scales (e.g., major, minor) which use seven distinct pitches.

14383.subject: Music
14383.question_text:
(i) Define interval inversion.
(ii) Invert the following intervals and state their new quality:
(a) Perfect 5th (C to G)
(b) Major 3rd (E to G#)
14383.explanation:
(i) Interval inversion occurs when the lower note of an interval is moved up an octave, or the upper note is moved down an octave, changing the interval's quality.
(ii) (a) A Perfect 5th inverts to a Perfect 4th (G to C).
(b) A Major 3rd inverts to a Minor 6th (G# to E).

14384.subject: Music
14384.question_text:
Write the first inversion of a C major triad in:
(i) Staff notation (treble clef)
(ii) Roman numeral analysis (using figured bass)
14384.explanation:
(i) The first inversion of a C major triad (C-E-G) is E-G-C, written with E on the bottom in the treble clef.
(ii) In Roman numeral analysis, it is labeled as I6 (or I6).

14385.subject: Music
14385.question_text: Which cadence is formed by the chord progression V - I?
14385.explanation: The V - I progression forms a perfect authentic cadence, which provides a strong sense of resolution in tonal music.

14386.subject: Music
14386.question_text: Describe three characteristic features of traditional African music and explain their significance.
14386.explanation:
(1) Call-and-response: A leader sings or plays a phrase, and a group responds, fostering community participation.
(2) Polyrhythms: Multiple conflicting rhythms create complexity and drive, common in drumming traditions.
(3) Oral tradition: Music is transmitted orally, preserving cultural heritage and adaptability.

14387.subject: Music
14387.question_text: Identify two Ghanaian traditional musical instruments and describe their roles in performance.
14387.explanation:
(1) Atumpan: A pair of talking drums used in Akan ceremonies to mimic speech tones and communicate messages.
(2) Gye Nyame: A thumb piano (lamellophone) used in recreational music to provide melodic accompaniment.

14388.subject: Music
14388.question_text:
Compose an 8-bar melody in the key of G major for the soprano voice, incorporating:
(i) A sequence
(ii) A climax
(iii) A balanced phrase structure
14388.explanation:
A valid melody should:
(i) Include a sequence (repetition of a motif at a different pitch).
(ii) Build to a climax (highest note) in bars 5-6.
(iii) Use balanced phrases (e.g., 2+2+4 bars) with clear cadences.

14389.subject: Music
14389.question_text: Which composer is not associated with the Classical period?
14389.explanation: Johann Sebastian Bach was a Baroque composer, while Mozart, Haydn, and Beethoven are key figures of the Classical period.
